verdict.rationale: Nix's docs say it runs on Linux and macOS and that development environments can be shared across machines, so the same workflow and config is supported on two of the three platforms. Nothing in the evidence documents native Windows support. The Docker image is a host-platform route, not a Windows capability of Nix itself. missing for 10: Windows support, evidence that the same config behaves identically across macOS and Linux, independent cross-platform corroboration

support.subject: As a developer, I can use the same workflow and config on macOS, Linux, and Windows

citations.quote: Runs on Linux and macOS, next to the package manager you already have.
Nix makes it trivial to share development and build environments for your projects, regardless of what programming languages and tools you're using.
if a package works on one machine, it will also work on another.
Easy transfer of software environments between computers.
